name: commons-threshold-2
description: ⭐ THE FIRST FALLBACK KNOB OF THE COMMONS, TURNED ON (C10, Dean 09/09/2026). rules.economy.commonsThreshold 2: a central board holding two cards REFUSES a third until somebody Harvests it. The shipped rule is null, no cap, and this is the arm that says what a cap would buy. ⛔ IT IS THE ONLY THING IN THE COMMONS THAT CAN REFUSE A PLAY, so this is a change to C4 ("central boards have no threshold; nothing in the game refuses a play") and not a tuning of it. Read it as a rules arm. WHY IT EXISTS BEFORE ANYBODY HAS ASKED FOR IT. The failure the commons is most likely to repeat is the one the meeple visit died of at a real table: THE BONUS READING AUTOMATIC. Dean, 09/09/2026 - "with a meeple always available the bonus was basically free". A meeple visit at least needed a meeple; a card play needs a card, and a hand almost always has one, so the commons is if anything MORE always-available than the thing it replaced. Dean's band is that the bonus should be played on 30% to 60% of turns; if a17 reads above 60% - at TWO PLAYERS first, which is where every rate in this game runs hottest - this arm is the next run. ⚠️ IT IS NOT THE v31 CLOG COMING BACK, and the difference is worth holding on to. A clogged v31 Notice Board was one player's board, shut by its owner, denying the table a suit action until that owner chose to spend a Harvest. A full central board shuts one of FIVE boards to EVERYBODY including whoever filled it, and ANY player may empty it with a Harvest and take the pile into their barn - so the cap creates a race for a full pile rather than a denial. ⭐ THAT IS THE SECOND-ORDER EFFECT TO WATCH, and it may be the real result of this arm: at 2 a full board is four cards for whoever Harvests first, which prices the Wheat board and the Harvest action upward and could move the barn glut and the farm-bypass reading more than it moves the bonus rate. READ IN THIS ORDER: (1) the bonus rate against the band; (2) the refusal rate - how often a seat wanted a board that was full, which is the blocked-want reading under a new name and read 8.1% at 2 players the last time a rule refused anything; (3) central harvests per player per game and the median pile size at harvest; (4) the door mix, because a cap redistributes traffic toward whichever boards nobody is filling. Sweep it against the shipped null and never in the same overlay as commons-colour-match-v1: the two ration different things and a joint move is unattributable.
